- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3 day lag correction, reducing forecast by 1–2% per day.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.00 or -0.33), model underperforms; apply upward bias to forecast to avoid mean reversion trap.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates in early periods (days 1–7) when sentiment is bullish; cap forecast at 1–2% below true outcome for first 7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment drops below 0.33 after day 10, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
